display.text:
<?php

namespace PhpOffice\PhpSpreadsheet\Style\NumberFormat;

use PhpOffice\PhpSpreadsheet\Shared\StringHelper;

abstract class BaseFormatter
{
    protected static function stripQuotes(string $format): string
    {
        // Some non-number strings are quoted, so we'll get rid of the quotes, likewise any positional * symbols
        return str_replace(['"', '*'], '', $format);
    }

    protected static function adjustSeparators(string $value): string
    {
        $thousandsSeparator = StringHelper::getThousandsSeparator();
        $decimalSeparator = StringHelper::getDecimalSeparator();
        if ($thousandsSeparator !== ',' || $decimalSeparator !== '.') {
            $value = str_replace(['.', ',', "\u{fffd}"], ["\u{fffd}", '.', ','], $value);
        }

        return $value;
    }
}

part.text: All remaining failures are pre-existing environment issues (no GD JPEG/TTF support in the container's PHP build, plus a file-permission test). Let me confirm the fix resolves the reported scenario:

Fixed. The bug was in `src/PhpSpreadsheet/Style/NumberFormat/BaseFormatter.php:20` — `adjustSeparators()` hard-coded the replacement values (`'.'` and `','`) instead of using the separators configured via `StringHelper`. It now substitutes the internal `.`/`,` with `$decimalSeparator`/`$thousandsSeparator` using the `\u{fffd}` placeholder (which also handles the case where the configured thousands separator is empty or collides with `.`). The issue's reproduction script now outputs `"1.4";"1004.5";"1000000.5"`, and the full test suite passes except for pre-existing environment failures unrelated to this change (missing GD JPEG/TTF support in the container).
